title: Shadi Anudan UP: Online Apply, Status, Eligibility
meta_description: Shadi Anudan UP gives Rs 20,000 for daughter's marriage to poor families. Apply at shadianudan.upsdc.gov.in. Income limit: Rs 46,080 rural, Rs 56,460 urban.

hero.one_liner: Shadi Anudan UP gives Rs 20,000 for a daughter's marriage to eligible poor families. Apply at shadianudan.upsdc.gov.in within 90 days of the wedding.

what_is_it: Shadi Anudan UP is a financial assistance scheme run by the Uttar Pradesh Social Welfare Department that provides a one-time grant of Rs 20,000 to economically weak families for the marriage of their daughters. The scheme operates through the official portal at shadianudan.upsdc.gov.in and the money is transferred directly to the applicant's Aadhaar-linked bank account through DBT.

The scheme covers families from all major categories including General, Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Other Backward Class, and Minority communities. The income of the family, not the caste alone, is the primary eligibility criterion, and both rural and urban families can benefit.

eligibility_filters.notes: UP families marrying a daughter aged 18+, income under Rs 46,080 rural or Rs 56,460 urban, max two daughters. Apply 90 days before to 90 days after the wedding on shadianudan.upsdc.gov.in. Category-wise links: SC/ST/General via Social Welfare, OBC via Backward Class Welfare, minorities via Minority Welfare.

how_to_apply.title: Open the official portal and select your category
how_to_apply.description: Visit shadianudan.upsdc.gov.in on a browser. On the home page, select your caste category from the registration options: 'Samanya, Anusuchit Jati, Anusuchit Janjaati' for General/SC/ST, 'Anya Picchda Varg' for OBC, or 'Alpasankhyak, Anyatam Picchda Varg' for Minority. Clicking the correct category link takes you to the relevant application form.

how_to_apply.title: Fill in the applicant and family details
how_to_apply.description: Enter the applicant's name, Aadhaar number, address, mobile number, and annual income. Enter the daughter's name, date of birth, and the scheduled or completed date of marriage. Confirm that the income is within the limit for your area (Rs 46,080 for rural, Rs 56,460 for urban). Double-check all entered details against original documents before proceeding.

how_to_apply.title: Upload required documents
how_to_apply.description: Upload scanned copies of the income certificate, applicant's Aadhaar card, daughter's Aadhaar card, caste certificate, and marriage date certificate. Files must be in JPG or PDF format and within the size limit specified on the portal. Ensure each uploaded scan is clear and all text is fully legible.

how_to_apply.title: Enter bank account details and submit
how_to_apply.description: Enter the bank account number and IFSC code of the Aadhaar-linked account to which the Rs 20,000 grant will be credited. Review the entire form once more for accuracy, accept the declaration, and click Submit. Note down or print the application reference number that appears on the screen after successful submission.

how_to_apply.title: Take printout and submit physical documents
how_to_apply.description: Print the submitted application form from the portal. Attach self-attested photocopies of all uploaded documents. Submit the printout and document copies to the Block Development Officer (BDO) in rural areas or the Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO/SDM) in urban areas. Obtain an acknowledgment receipt from the office. This physical submission step is mandatory.

how_to_apply.title: Track application status online
how_to_apply.description: After a few days, visit shadianudan.upsdc.gov.in and go to 'Avedan ki Sthiti' (Application Status). Enter your application reference number and select your category to check the processing stage. If the status shows 'Under Verification' for more than 30 days after physical submission, follow up at the BDO or SDO office in person.

ministry: Social Welfare Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh

extra_sections.heading: What Is Shadi Anudan UP
content: The income ceiling for rural applicants is Rs 46,080 per year, and for urban applicants it is Rs 56,460 per year. These income limits apply to the total annual income of the entire family, not just the head of the household.

To be eligible for the scheme, the daughter being married must be at least 18 years old at the time of marriage. The groom must be at least 21 years of age, in line with India's legally mandated minimum marriage ages.
A single family can receive the Shadi Anudan grant for a maximum of two daughters. If a family has three or more daughters, only the first two marriages can be covered under this scheme.

The application window is 90 days before the marriage date to 90 days after the marriage date. Applications submitted earlier or later than this window will not be processed, so families must keep track of the timeline relative to the wedding date.
Each file should be in JPG or PDF format within the size limit specified on shadianudan.upsdc.gov.in. Applicants should check the file size requirements on the portal before scanning and uploading.

extra_sections.heading: More Details and Coverage
content: The Department of Social Welfare in each district has a designated officer for Shadi Anudan queries and unresolved applications. Families with delayed or rejected applications should approach this officer directly for assistance.
Contact details for district social welfare offices are available at samajkalyan.up.gov.in. An in-person visit to the district office is often the most effective way to resolve a stalled application.

Applicants should retain copies of all submitted documents, including the BDO or SDO acknowledgment receipt, for at least one year after payment. These copies serve as evidence in case of any future audit or dispute regarding the grant.

extra_sections.title: Shadi Anudan Is Not CM Samuhik Vivah
extra_sections.content:
Shadi Anudan gives Rs 20,000 in cash to a family for their own private wedding. CM Samuhik Vivah is a separate scheme that organises mass weddings.

They are run by different portals. A family can in principle benefit from both if it meets each scheme's rules, but they are not the same thing.

extra_sections.heading: Who Is Eligible
content: The 90-day pre-marriage window allows families to plan ahead and arrange the grant before the wedding expenses arise. The 90-day post-marriage window accommodates families who were unaware of the scheme or faced difficulties applying in time.

Different caste categories have different administering departments, but all applications are primarily initiated through the main portal at shadianudan.upsdc.gov.in. General category and Scheduled Caste families are covered by the Social Welfare Department (Samaj Kalyan Vibhag).

OBC families must apply through the Backward Class Welfare Department at backwardwelfareup.gov.in. Minority families apply through the Minority Welfare Department, and ST families through the Tribal Development Department.
All categories follow the same income limits and eligibility criteria under Shadi Anudan. The only difference is the administering department, which changes based on the applicant's caste category.

The UP government periodically publishes beneficiary lists for Shadi Anudan Yojana. These district-wise lists are accessible through the portal and allow families to verify whether their application has been formally approved and included in the disbursement list.

extra_sections.heading: The Income Limits and Categories
content: The primary portal shadianudan.upsdc.gov.in provides category-wise application links. Applicants should first determine their category and then select the correct registration form from the portal's home page to ensure the application reaches the right department.

The Rs 20,000 Shadi Anudan grant is separate from the Mukhyamantri Samuhik Vivah Yojana. CM Samuhik Vivah involves government-organised collective weddings where each couple receives approximately Rs 51,000 in goods and cash.

Shadi Anudan is an individual cash grant for families arranging their own private wedding. The two schemes are run by the same department but have different portals and different application processes.

Families can in principle benefit from both schemes if they meet the eligibility criteria of each and participate in the respective processes. However, the CM Samuhik Vivah scheme requires the couple to attend a government-organised collective ceremony, while Shadi Anudan is for individual weddings.

The annual budget for Shadi Anudan is approved during the UP state budget session and applications are processed in order of receipt within this allocation. Once the annual budget is exhausted, pending applications carry forward to the next financial year.

extra_sections.heading: The 90-Day Application Window
content: The application process begins with online registration on shadianudan.upsdc.gov.in. The applicant fills in personal details, family details, income information, and bank account details, then uploads scanned copies of the required documents.
After online submission, the portal generates an application reference number. This number is essential for checking the application status and must be noted or printed immediately after submission.

The online submission alone does not complete the Shadi Anudan application. A printed copy of the filled form along with self-attested copies of all supporting documents must be physically submitted to the Block Development Officer (BDO) in rural areas or the Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO/SDM) in urban areas.

The physical document submission is mandatory because it allows the concerned officer to conduct a ground-level verification of the applicant's details and the marriage. The officer will issue an acknowledgment receipt upon receiving the physical documents.

Families who apply early in the financial year, ideally between April and July, have a better chance of being processed within the current year's budget. Late applications in January to March may face delays if the budget is nearly spent.

extra_sections.title: Apply Before or After the Wedding
extra_sections.desc:
You can apply from 90 days before the marriage date to 90 days after it. Applications outside this window are rejected.

Applying early, in the pre-marriage window, lets families arrange the grant before wedding expenses arise. Apply early in the financial year for faster processing.

extra_sections.heading: How to Apply Online
content: Documents required for Shadi Anudan include an income certificate, the Aadhaar card of the applicant, the Aadhaar card of the daughter being married, a caste certificate, and a marriage date certificate. The income certificate must be issued by a competent revenue authority such as a lekhpal, SDM, or tehsildar.

The marriage date certificate is used to verify that the application falls within the 90-day window. It can be a certificate from the local Gram Pradhan, Ward Sabhasad, or Lekhpal in the absence of a formal registered marriage document.

Formal marriage registration documents such as a Vivah Panjikaran certificate, if available, can also be used as proof of marriage date. However, the scheme does not require the marriage to be formally registered at the time of application.

The bank account provided for DBT must be in the name of the applicant (head of household) and linked to their Aadhaar. A bank account that is not Aadhaar-linked will prevent the DBT payment from being processed.

The scheme does not cover marriages of sons. It is specifically designed for the marriage of daughters in recognition of the traditionally higher financial burden associated with a daughter's wedding in many communities across Uttar Pradesh.

steps.desc: On shadianudan.upsdc.gov.in, choose your category. SC, ST, and General go via Social Welfare, OBC via Backward Class Welfare, minorities via Minority Welfare.

steps.desc: Online submission alone is not enough. Print the form, attach documents, and submit to the BDO in rural areas or the SDM/city magistrate in urban areas.

steps.title: Verification and DBT
steps.desc: After ground verification, Rs 20,000 is credited to the applicant's Aadhaar-linked bank account.

extra_sections.heading: Documents and Physical Submission
content: Applicants who do not have an Aadhaar-linked bank account should visit their bank branch with their Aadhaar card and complete the Aadhaar seeding process before applying for Shadi Anudan. The process typically takes two to three working days.

The bank account should be with a nationalised or scheduled commercial bank. The grant amount of Rs 20,000 will be credited within a few weeks of approval, depending on the volume of applications being processed by the district.

The status of an application can be tracked at shadianudan.upsdc.gov.in by visiting the 'Avedan ki Sthiti' or Application Status section. The applicant enters the application number and selects the category to view the current processing stage.

The status typically shows stages such as 'Submitted', 'Under Verification', 'Verified', 'Approved', and 'Payment Credited'. Applications stuck at 'Under Verification' for more than 30 days should be followed up with the BDO or SDO office.

The Shadi Anudan grant does not affect a family's eligibility for other government benefits such as ration cards, old age pensions, widow pensions, or housing schemes. It is an additional welfare measure and is independent of other scheme benefits.

extra_sections.heading: Checking Status and Rejections
content: Common reasons for rejection include income exceeding the prescribed limit, application submitted outside the 90-day window, mismatched names across documents, invalid Aadhaar details, or missing caste certificate. Rejected applications display the reason for rejection in the status section.

Applicants can correct and resubmit their applications after addressing the rejection reason, provided the 90-day application window is still active. Applications rejected due to the window expiry cannot be resubmitted for the same marriage.

The Uttar Pradesh government also runs a grievance portal at jansunwai.up.nic.in where applicants who have not received payment within 60 days of approval can raise a formal complaint. The portal mandates a departmental response and follow-up within a set timeline.

Applicants who lack internet access or are unfamiliar with online processes can visit a Common Service Centre (CSC), also known as Jan Seva Kendra, for assistance. CSC operators can fill and submit the Shadi Anudan application on behalf of the family and guide them through the document upload steps.

Families in urban areas are fully eligible for Shadi Anudan, with the income ceiling set slightly higher at Rs 56,460 per year compared to Rs 46,080 for rural families. The online application form and document requirements are identical for both.

extra_sections.title: Use Only the Official Portal
extra_sections.content:
Fake Shadi Anudan websites exist. The only official portal is shadianudan.upsdc.gov.in. Do not submit personal or bank details on any lookalike site.

Common rejection reasons are income above the limit, applying outside the window, or a name mismatch across documents. Fix the reason and resubmit within the window.

extra_sections.heading: Common Reasons for Rejection
content: CSC assistance is usually available at a nominal charge. However, if any CSC operator or agent demands a large fee or claims to guarantee faster approval, the applicant should report this to the district Social Welfare Office as such facilitation charges beyond nominal CSC rates are not officially sanctioned.

The scheme has been operational in Uttar Pradesh for many years and has undergone significant improvements in transparency since the government moved to fully online applications. The DBT mechanism ensures that the grant reaches the intended beneficiary without any middleman deductions.

A widow or single mother can apply as the head of the household for her daughter's marriage grant. The scheme does not require the father of the bride to be the applicant; any legal guardian or head of the family who meets the income criteria can apply.

The scheme does not restrict the type of marriage ceremony. Families from all religious communities can apply, whether the wedding is a religious ceremony, a court marriage, or any other socially recognised form.

The key difference for urban applicants is the physical document submission point. Urban families submit their printed form and document copies to the Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO) rather than the Block Development Officer (BDO).

extra_sections.text: For a family earning Rs 3,500 per month in rural UP, the Shadi Anudan grant of Rs 20,000 represents nearly six months of income. Direct bank transfer ensures the full amount reaches the family without any deduction, making it one of the most impactful single-payment welfare measures for daughters' marriages in the state.

extra_sections.heading: Grievances and District Support
content: What matters is meeting the income and age eligibility criteria, not the form of the marriage. Hindu, Muslim, Christian, Sikh, and other community families are all equally eligible.

Applicants should ensure that the name on the Aadhaar card exactly matches the name on the income certificate and caste certificate. Even a minor spelling difference between documents is a common cause of application delay or rejection.

If the name on the Aadhaar card is different from the name on other documents, the applicant should first get the name corrected in the Aadhaar database through the official UIDAI process before submitting the Shadi Anudan application.
Document scans uploaded online must be clear and legible to pass the initial digital verification. Blurry, overexposed, or incomplete scans are a common cause of early rejection.

The scheme also aligns with national goals of eliminating child marriage. By requiring the bride to be at least 18 and the groom to be at least 21, the Shadi Anudan Yojana reinforces legal minimum marriage ages and discourages families from marrying daughters off before the required age.

extra_sections.heading: What Else to Know
content: For minority families, the Waqf Board or minority welfare district officer can sometimes assist with documentation and the application process. The Minority Welfare Department also runs awareness camps in select districts to help minority families apply for Shadi Anudan and related schemes.

The grant amount of Rs 20,000 is meaningful for families earning below the poverty line. For a family with an annual income of Rs 30,000 to Rs 40,000, this represents a significant fraction of their yearly earnings and directly reduces wedding-related debt.

The scheme, together with CM Samuhik Vivah Yojana, reflects the Uttar Pradesh government's commitment to providing financial protection to economically vulnerable families at the critical life event of a daughter's marriage. Families are encouraged to use both schemes if eligible for each.

extra_sections.title: Practical Tips and Process
extra_sections.content:
The scheme is periodically audited by the state government to ensure that only genuine beneficiaries receive the grant. Families found to have submitted false income certificates or inflated their eligibility may face recovery of the grant amount and further action.

IT infrastructure improvements made to shadianudan.upsdc.gov.in over recent years have reduced processing times significantly. Most applications that are submitted correctly with complete documents are now processed within 30 to 45 days of physical document submission.

Applicants who face repeated website errors or technical issues on the portal can contact the district Social Welfare Office directly. The office can initiate the application manually on behalf of the applicant in exceptional cases of technical difficulty.

faqs.question: What is Shadi Anudan UP?
faqs.answer: Shadi Anudan UP is a Uttar Pradesh government scheme that provides a one-time grant of Rs 20,000 to economically weak families for the marriage of their daughters. It covers General, SC, ST, OBC, and Minority families with annual income below Rs 46,080 (rural) or Rs 56,460 (urban). Applications are submitted at shadianudan.upsdc.gov.in.

faqs.question: How much money does Shadi Anudan UP give?
faqs.answer: Shadi Anudan UP gives Rs 20,000 as a one-time grant per daughter, transferred directly to the applicant's Aadhaar-linked bank account through DBT. This is separate from the CM Samuhik Vivah Yojana, which provides a larger Rs 51,000 package through collective wedding events.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for Shadi Anudan UP?
faqs.answer: Eligible applicants must be permanent residents of Uttar Pradesh with annual family income below Rs 46,080 (rural) or Rs 56,460 (urban). The daughter must be at least 18 years old and the groom at least 21. All caste categories including General, SC, ST, OBC, and Minority are covered, with a maximum of two daughters per family.

faqs.question: When should I apply for Shadi Anudan UP?
faqs.answer: You can apply from 90 days before the marriage date up to 90 days after the marriage date. Applications submitted outside this window are rejected. It is advisable to apply as early as possible within the window to allow time for verification and processing.

faqs.question: What documents are needed for Shadi Anudan UP?
faqs.answer: Required documents are: income certificate (from lekhpal, SDM, or tehsildar), applicant's Aadhaar card, daughter's Aadhaar card, caste certificate, and a marriage date certificate from Gram Pradhan or Lekhpal. The applicant's bank account must be Aadhaar-linked for DBT payment.

faqs.question: How do I apply for Shadi Anudan UP online?
faqs.answer: Visit shadianudan.upsdc.gov.in, select the registration link for your caste category, fill in the application form, upload required documents, enter bank details, and submit. After online submission, print the form and physically submit it with document copies to the BDO (rural) or SDO (urban) office. Both steps are mandatory.

faqs.question: How do I check Shadi Anudan UP application status?
faqs.answer: Go to shadianudan.upsdc.gov.in and click on 'Avedan ki Sthiti' (Application Status). Enter your application reference number and select your category to view the current processing stage. If stuck at verification for more than 30 days, follow up at your BDO or SDO office.

faqs.question: Is Shadi Anudan the same as CM Samuhik Vivah Yojana?
faqs.answer: No. Shadi Anudan Yojana (shadianudan.upsdc.gov.in) gives Rs 20,000 cash for your own private wedding. CM Samuhik Vivah Yojana (cmsvy.upsdc.gov.in) provides about Rs 51,000 in goods and cash through government-organised collective wedding events. Both are from the Social Welfare Department but are different schemes with different portals.

faqs.question: Can OBC families apply for Shadi Anudan UP?
faqs.answer: Yes, OBC families are fully eligible for Shadi Anudan UP, but their applications are processed by the Backward Class Welfare Department rather than the Social Welfare Department. OBC applicants should use the OBC registration link at shadianudan.upsdc.gov.in, which redirects to the Backward Class Welfare portal.

faqs.question: How long does it take to receive Shadi Anudan payment?
faqs.answer: Payment is typically credited within 30 to 45 days of the BDO or SDO verifying and approving the physical documents. If payment is not received within 60 days of approval, raise a grievance at jansunwai.up.nic.in for departmental follow-up.
